3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that, the pond originally belonged to one Girish Chandra Mohajan who died leaving 4 sons namely, Nishi Chandra, Ram Chandra, Mahendra Lal and Manindra Lal and also a grandson namely, Profullah Kumar, son of Jogesh Chandra who predeceased Girish Chandra Mohajan. The heirs of Girish Chandra Mohajan settled the pond with the plaintiffs namely, Jeabat Ali and Ayub Ali at a rental of Taka 8.00 about 25 years back and since then the plaintiffs have been possessing the said pond and its bank. Defendant No. 38, Profullah Kumar gave out that he got the suit pond in his share by amicable settlement amongst the co-sharers. The defendant No. 37, Manindra Lal Mohajan who acted as Karjakarak on behalf of the co-sharers admitted the alleged facts. In fact, the plaintiffs took permanent settlement of the said pond from Profulla (defendant No. 38) by two registered pattas to the extent of 16 gondas (8 gondas each) and one Dudu Meah took settlement of the remaining 6 gondas of the said pond by another registered patta. Dudu Meah, thereafter, sold his share to the plaintiff No.1 i.e. the present petitioner herein by registered Kabala wherein the defendant No. 2 Fazal Karim alias Fazal Ahamed was an attesting witness. The plaintiffs continued their exclusive possession in the suit pond and its bank. They also constructed a cow shed and planted fruit bearing trees. The plaintiff No. 1 also buried dead body of his wife in the bank of the said pond. As such, the plaintiffs acquired the exclusive title in the suit pond and continuing their possession for more than 12 years before the institution of the suit and also acquired title by adverse possession. 

 20. Abdul Gani has also deposed as DW 2 at the trial Court wherein he has admitted in cross-examination that 'about three years back the grave of mother of Ayub was placed at the northern bank of the pond" but he did not say anything with regard to amicable settlement or partition. The plaintiff-petitioner did not produce any witness at the appellate stage. The learned Appellate Court on the basis of the evidence of DWs 1 and 2 taken at the appellate stage disposed of the appeal holding that thee had been no amicable settlement or partition amongst the co-sharers of Girish Chandra Mohajan and therefore, the plaintiffs' declaration with regard to title and confirmation of possession on the basis of registered pattas exhibit 2 and 2(A) cannot be given in favour of the plaintiffs. The Appellate Court observed that the plaintiffs may get at best declaration of the title in respect of 1/5th share of the suit property i.e. 1/5th share of Profullah. The learned Appellate Court further held that since the plaintiffs have been claiming that there had been amicable settlement of the property of Girish Chandra Mohajan and since the plaintiffs failed to prove the said amicable settlement, they are not entitled to the relief as prayed for. 

 "The suit land is pond. It belonged to Girish Chandra Mohajan. He died leaving Nishi, Ram Chandra, Mohendra Ch. J ogesh Ch. Manindra. Jogesh died leaving son Profulla. All the 5 sons settled the suit land from year to year on a jama of Rs.8.00 per year about 25/26 years back. We possessed then for 8/11 years on payment of rents to Monindra Mohajan who was Karayakarak of all the 3 brothers. 2 dakhilas are filed. This dakhila was signed and written by Monindra. This is marked Ext. 1. On the 9th year Manindra said that the pond (in suit) fell in the share of ProfulIa by amicable settlement and the rents paid to him. For 2 years we paid rents to him. Then Profulla said that he would settle it permanently. Then my father & myself took settlement of the pond in suit having 8 gandas. The pattas were written by Saleh Ahmed & Oli Mia and executed by Profulla by signing his name himself. These are marked Ext. 2 & 2(a). On that date Profulla also settled 6 gandas of land of suit land. We paid consideration money. The patta in favour of Dudu was written by Saleh Ahmed and executed by Profulla. A consideration money of Rs. 95.00 was paid by him in my presence. This is marked Ext. 2(b). I again purchased the share of Dudu Mia after his possession for 718 years. The kabala was written by Mohendra and executed by Dudu Mia by putting his thumb impression. Imam Baksh wrote his name. I paid the consideration money (This is Ext. 3). 

 Then Profulla settled the land on behalf of all the brothers by amicable settlement in his share from other brothers to plffs & Dudu Mia. I was an attesting witness of the 2 pattas. The plffs & Dudu Mia gave Nazar Selami to Profulla. Dudu Mia then after 7/8 years sold his share to Ayub Ali. Since then plffs have been possessing. The defdts or anybody did not possess the suit land during last 25/26 years, but the plffs possessed it all along. 

 28. Mr. Khondoker has next argued alternatively, that the trial Court was fully justified in decreeing the suit on the basis of pleading of adverse possession and a prayer made to the effect, Mr. Khondoker submits that the Appellate Court having failed to avert to that aspect of the judgment of the trial Court has also committed an error of law in deciding the appeal and there has been failure of justice. The Appellate Court in its judgment has stated that since that claim of the plaintiffs are mainly based on pattas settlement obtained from Profulla and since the plaintiffs failed to prove the amicable settlement the plaintiff cannot get declaration in his favour as prayed for on the basis of adverse possession. It is on record that the plaintiffs in their pleading in paragraph 9 of the plaint has set up an alternative claim of title by adverse possession followed by a prayer in para 'Ka' of the prayer portion, and the trial Court decreed the suit on the basis of adverse possession on consideration of evidence of PWs. 1-9. 

 29. I have given careful consideration of the evidence of PWs as well as DWs. The plaintiffs though have set out in paragraph 9 of the plaint an alternative claim of title on the basis of adverse possession nevertheless the plaintiffs have not led any specific evidence with regard to adverse possession except to say that PWs have claimed to have possessed the suit pond continuously for more than 20/25 years. But there is no evidence that they were possessing openly to the knowledge of the rightful owners. The plaintiffs claim over the suit pond is on the basis of pattas given by Profulla and by purchase from Dudu Mia. Therefore, the case of adverse possession as required under law has not been made out. On this point Mr. Khademul Islam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of defendant No. 1. Opposite party has placed reliance on the decision of P Lakshmi Reddy vs. L Lakshmi Reddy reported in AIR 1957 (SC) 314 wherein it has been held that the possession required must be adequate in continuity, in publicity and in extent to show that it is in possession adverse to the competitor. It has been further held that it is well settled that in order to establish adverse possession of one co-heir as against another it is not enough to show that one out of them is in sole possession and enjoyment of the profits of the properties. Ouster of the non-possessing co-heir by the co-heir in possession who claims his possession to be adverse, should be made out. The possession of one co-heir is considered in law as possession of all the co-heirs. When one co-heir is found to be in possession of the properties it is presumed to be on the basis of joint title. The co-heir in possession cannot render his possession adverse to the other co-heirs, not in possession, merely by any secret hostile animus on his own part in derogation of the other co-heirs title. It is a settled rule of law that as between co-heirs there must be evidence of open assertion of hostile title, coupled with exclusive possession and enjoyment by one of them to the knowledge of the other so as to constitute ouster. Mr. Khademul Islam Chowdhury submits that there is no evidence of open assertion of hostile title coupled with exclusive possession and enjoyment by one of them to the knowledge of others. In this particular case he submits that the basis of the claim of the plaintiffs is clearly amicable settlement and taking pattas settlement from one of the co-sharers of Girish Chandra Mohajan. He submits that the result of the case depends on as to whether there has been in fact an amicable partition of properties of Girish Chandra Mohajan. I find force in the submission of Mr. Khademul Islam Chowdhury. The plaintiffs did not make out a case of adverse possession inasmuch as there is no evidence on record as to publicity and in extent to show that the plaintiffs were possessing adversely against the competitors. 

 30. The definite case of the plaintiffs is that, ever since their obtaining the patta settlement from Profulla they are in possession of the suit pond. Since I have already held that there are enough evidence on record to come to a finding that there has been amicable partition of the properties of Girish Chandra Mohajan, the settlement obtained by the plaintiffs from Profulla by pattas is valid and legal and the plaintiffs are entitled to a decree as prayed for on the basis of pattas Ext. 2 and 2(A). Besides, the circumstantial evidence is also in favour of the plaintiffs. Nobody contested the appeal except the defendant No.1 No one is coming to contest the revision except the defendant No.1, who alleged to have purchased to the extent of one ganda from Manindra. In that view of the matter I am inclined to hold that the judgment and decree passed by the Appellate Court is liable to be set aside and the plaintiffs are entitled to a decree as prayed for on the basis of settlement by registered pattas Exts.2 and 2 (A) and by purchase from Dudu Mia and not by adverse possession.
